chunks: 4940 - And it is narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Jābir, from Zaynab bint ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
Fāṭimah عليها السلام said in her sermon concerning the matter of Fadak:

Allah has among you a covenant that He advanced to you, and a remainder that He appointed over you: the Book of Allah, whose insights are clear, whose signs are evident, whose inner meanings are unveiled, and whose outward proofs are manifest. Its hearing is enduring for creation; it leads its followers to good pleasure and brings its adherents to salvation. In it is the clarification of Allah’s illuminated proofs, His defined prohibitions, His recommended virtues, His sufficient summaries, His granted dispensations, His prescribed laws, and His clear evidences. So Allah made faith a purification from shirk, salat (prayer) a cleansing from arrogance, zakat an increase in provision, fasting a clarification of sincerity, hajj a strengthening of the religion, justice a settling of hearts, obedience an order for the community, Imamate a uniting against division, jihad an honor for Islam, patience an aid toward seeking response, enjoining what is right a benefit for the public, dutifulness to parents a protection against wrath, maintaining kinship ties a cause of increase in number, legal retribution a preservation of blood, fulfillment of vows an exposure to forgiveness, giving full measure and weights a reproach against deficiency, slandering chaste women a barrier from curse, abandoning theft an obligation of chastity, consuming the wealth of orphans a protection from wrongdoing, justice in judgments a reassurance for the subjects; and Allah has forbidden shirk as sincerity to Him in Lordship.
So fear Allah as He should truly be feared.
Regarding what Allah has commanded you with, and desist from what He has forbidden you.

key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: Zakat, ordained as a cause of increase in provision.
key_terms.الشِّرْكَ: Shirk, forbidden so that devotion in Lordship remains purely for Allah.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: Salat (prayer), prescribed as purification from arrogance.
key_terms.الصِّيَامَ: Fasting, prescribed as a manifestation of sincerity.
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةَ: Imamate, established as a means of uniting against division.
key_terms.الْإِيمَانَ: Faith, ordained as purification from shirk.
key_terms.الْعَدْلَ: Justice, described as a source of calm for hearts and reassurance for subjects.
key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: The Book of Allah as the divine covenant, proof, and source of guidance.

ai.seo_question: How does Sayyidah Fāṭimah عليها السلام explain the wisdom behind faith, salat, zakat, fasting, hajj, justice, and Imamate?
ai.summary: This sermon of Sayyidah Fāṭimah عليها السلام presents the Book of Allah as the enduring divine covenant and source of guidance, law, and proof. It then outlines the wisdom behind major obligations and prohibitions, showing how faith, worship, justice, Imamate, and moral conduct preserve both religion and society. The passage concludes with a Quranic call to taqwa and obedience to Allah’s commands.
